title: Why Does Spinning Make You Dizzy?
description:
Why Does Spinning Make You Dizzy?
A Pip and Ray science short. Educational, not medical advice.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Whoa whoa whoa... why is the room STILL spinning?! I STOPPED!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: The room stopped. Your ears didn't.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: My EARS?! I'm dizzy... not deaf!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Deep inside each ear, you have three tiny loops... the semicircular canals. And they're full of fluid. Watch...

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: When you spin, that fluid lags behind... and bends tiny hairs inside the loop. That bend tells your brain: we're SPINNING!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Keep spinning, and the fluid catches up. The hairs straighten... and your brain thinks everything is still.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Okay... so what happens when I STOP?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: The fluid keeps going! It bends the hairs the OTHER way... so your brain hears SPINNING, while your eyes see STILL.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: That mixed signal... IS the dizziness.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: So I just... wait for my ear juice to stop sloshing?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Ha! Exactly! A few seconds, the fluid settles, the hairs straighten... and the world stops spinning.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: My ears are basically two tiny cups of coffee!
